tasks.title: Ready<T>
tasks.statement: Write a future struct Ready<T>(Option<T>) implementing Future<Output = T>: the first poll returns the value.
tasks.hint: self.0.take() takes the value out of the Option.

tasks.title: YieldOnce
tasks.statement: Write YieldOnce { done: bool }: the first poll calls cx.waker().wake_by_ref() and returns Pending, the second returns Ready(()).
tasks.hint: The done state changes on the first poll.

tasks.title: CountDown
tasks.statement: Write CountDown(u32): while the counter is above zero, each poll decrements it and returns Pending (with wake_by_ref); when it reaches zero, return Ready("поехали").
tasks.hint: Do not forget wake_by_ref before Pending.

tasks.title: Poll counter
tasks.statement: Write a wrapper Counted<F> { inner: Pin<Box<F>>, polls: u32 }: each poll increments polls and polls inner; a method polls(&self) -> u32. The driver wraps CountDown and reports the number of polls.
tasks.hint: inner: Pin<Box<F>> can be polled via as_mut().poll(cx); the struct is Unpin (Pin<Box<…>> is always Unpin), so its fields are reachable through self.get_mut().

tasks.title: Map
tasks.statement: Write a combinator Map<F, G> { inner: Pin<Box<F>>, f: Option<G> }: poll polls inner; when it is ready, it applies the function f (once) and returns the result.
tasks.hint: Pass the result of inner to f.take().unwrap().

tasks.title: Sequence
tasks.statement: Write a combinator function then<A, B, FB>(a: A, f: impl FnOnce(A::Output) -> FB) -> impl Future<Output = B::Output>: first wait for a, then run the future that f returns (an async block).
tasks.hint: async move { let v = a.await; f(v).await }

tasks.title: Join2
tasks.statement: Write Join2<A, B> { a: Pin<Box<A>>, b: Pin<Box<B>>, ra: Option<A::Output>, rb: Option<B::Output> }: poll polls the parts that are not ready yet and returns a pair when both are ready.
tasks.hint: Poll only the parts without a result; the pair is ready when both are Some.

tasks.title: Select2
tasks.statement: Write Select2<A, B>: poll polls a, then b; it returns Either::Left(a's value) or Either::Right(b's value), whichever is ready first (if both are ready at once, a).
tasks.hint: Poll a, then b; the first Ready wins.

tasks.title: Your own block_on
tasks.statement: Write block_on<F: Future>(f: F) -> F::Output: pin the future (Box::pin), create a Context with Waker::noop() and poll in a loop until it is ready.
tasks.hint: Waker::noop() is a dummy waker (Rust ≥ 1.85).

tasks.title: block_on with park
tasks.statement: Write block_on_park<F: Future>(f: F) -> F::Output: the waker must wake the current thread (thread::unpark); implement the Wake trait for a struct holding a Thread; after Pending the loop calls thread::park().
tasks.hint: ThreadWaker::wake is self.0.unpark(); loop: Ready → return, Pending → park.

tasks.title: Your own timer
tasks.statement: Write Delay { shared: Arc<Mutex<Shared>> }: new(ms) spawns a thread that after ms milliseconds sets a flag and wakes the stored waker. poll: if the flag is set, Ready(()); otherwise save cx.waker().clone() and return Pending.
tasks.hint: The timer thread writes to the shared state and wakes the waker.

tasks.title: Your own oneshot
tasks.statement: Implement a oneshot channel: fn channel<T>() -> (Sender<T>, Receiver<T>); Sender::send(self, v) stores the value and wakes the receiver's waker; Receiver is a Future<Output = Option<T>> (None if the Sender is dropped without sending).
tasks.hint: Drop for Sender marks the channel closed and wakes the receiver.

tasks.title: Event between threads
tasks.statement: A struct Signal { inner: Arc<Mutex<(bool, Option<Waker>)>> }: the method fire(&self) sets the flag and wakes; Signal is Clone and is a Future<Output = ()>. The driver polls the future before and after fire.
tasks.hint: The flag and the waker live under one mutex.

tasks.title: Counting waker
tasks.statement: Implement a struct CountWake { n: AtomicUsize } with the Wake trait (wake and wake_by_ref increment n). The driver creates Waker::from(arc), polls YieldOnce and CountDown-like futures, and prints the number of wakeups.
tasks.hint: n.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) in both methods.

tasks.title: One poll
tasks.statement: Write poll_once<F: Future + Unpin>(f: &mut F) -> Option<F::Output>: poll the future once with Waker::noop(): Some(value) on Ready, None on Pending.
tasks.hint: Pin::new(f) is allowed for Unpin futures.

tasks.title: A manual state machine
tasks.statement: Write by hand a state machine TwoSteps equivalent to async { YieldOnce.await; YieldOnce.await; a + b } for a = 10 and b = 5: an enum of states Start, First, Second, Done; poll moves from state to state, returning Pending after each YieldOnce, and finally Ready(15).
tasks.hint: Each .await is a transition to the next state.

tasks.title: Async iterator
tasks.statement: The trait AsyncIter { type Item; fn poll_next(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx) -> Poll<Option<Item>> } is declared. Implement it for Ticks { left: u32, yielded: bool }: alternate Pending (once before each item) and the value left, left−1, …, 1, then Ready(None).
tasks.hint: Pending before each item, then Some(left).

tasks.title: Executor with a queue
tasks.statement: Write Executor { queue: VecDeque<Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()>>>> }: spawn(fut) enqueues a task; run() polls tasks in turn (Waker::noop()), putting Pending tasks back at the end, until the queue is empty.
tasks.hint: A task that returned Pending goes to the end of the queue.

tasks.title: Executor with results
tasks.statement: Write run_all<T>(futs: Vec<Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = T>>>>) -> Vec<T>: poll the futures that are not ready in a round-robin (Waker::noop()) and return the results in input order.
tasks.hint: Keep results in a Vec<Option<T>> and count how many remain.

tasks.title: Timeout by poll count
tasks.statement: Write Timeout<F> { inner: Pin<Box<F>>, left: u32 }: each poll decrements left; if inner is ready, Ok(value); if left is exhausted and inner is still Pending, Err("таймаут").
tasks.hint: Poll inner first; if it is Pending, check the remaining attempts.

tasks.title: pin!
tasks.statement: Write run_pinned<F: Future>(f: F) -> F::Output: pin the future on the stack with the std::pin::pin! macro (no Box) and poll it with Waker::noop() until it is ready.
tasks.hint: let mut f = std::pin::pin!(f); then f.as_mut().poll(…).

tasks.title: State machine size
tasks.statement: Write sizes() -> (usize, usize): size_of_val of two async blocks: small just returns 1; big holds an array [0u8; 1024] across an .await. The driver checks that big ≥ 1024 and small < 64.
tasks.hint: size_of_val(&async_block) is the size of the state machine.

tasks.title: Recursion with Box::pin
tasks.statement: Write sum_to(n: u64) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = u64>>>: the sum 1…n via a recursive async block (an .await on sum_to(n − 1)); sum_to(0) = 0.
tasks.hint: A recursive async fn is impossible without boxing: the state machine's size would be infinite.

tasks.title: JoinAll
tasks.statement: Write JoinAll<F: Future> { futs: Vec<Pin<Box<F>>>, results: Vec<Option<F::Output>> }: poll polls the parts that are not ready and returns a Vec of results in input order when all are ready.
tasks.hint: If all parts are ready, collect the results in input order.

tasks.title: async fn in a trait
tasks.statement: Declare trait Source { async fn get(&self) -> u32; }; implement it for Const(u32) (returns the number) and Delayed(u32) (one YieldOnce, then the number). The function total(a: &impl Source, b: &impl Source) -> u32 adds the results.
tasks.hint: async fn in traits is stable (Rust ≥ 1.75).

tasks.title: Cancel = drop
tasks.statement: A struct Job { name: String, steps: u32 } is a Future<Output = ()>: each poll decrements steps and returns Pending; at steps == 0 it is Ready. Implement Drop: it prints "drop <name> (steps=<left>)". The driver polls the Job once and drops it.
tasks.hint: Drop runs both on cancellation and on normal completion.

tasks.title: Fuse
tasks.statement: Write Fuse<F> { inner: Option<Pin<Box<F>>> }: after inner has returned Ready, further polls return Pending (and do not panic): the inner future is dropped.
tasks.hint: After Ready, replace inner with None.

tasks.title: Do not clone needlessly
tasks.statement: A struct WakerSlot { w: Option<Waker> } with a method register(&mut self, new: &Waker) -> bool: if the stored waker does not wake the same task (will_wake), replace it with a clone and return true; otherwise false (without cloning).
tasks.hint: Waker::will_wake tells whether two wakers wake the same task.

tasks.title: Executor with wakers
tasks.statement: Write a real executor: Executor { tx: SyncSender<Arc<Task>>, rx: Receiver<Arc<Task>> }. Task { fut: Mutex<Option<Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send>>>>, tx: SyncSender<Arc<Task>> }; spawn creates a task and sends it to the queue; Wake for Task sends itself to the queue; run() processes the queue until the signal arrives (the outer tx is dropped) and the tasks are finished.
tasks.hint: The queue is a sync_channel; in run: drop(self.tx), so the loop ends once all tasks give up their copies of tx.

tasks.title: Collect an async iterator
tasks.statement: The trait AsyncIter is declared. Write collect_all<S: AsyncIter + Unpin>(mut s: S) -> Vec<S::Item>: poll poll_next with Waker::noop() in a loop (skip Pending) until None.
tasks.hint: Pin::new(&mut s) is allowed because S: Unpin.
